———————————————————————————

----------
It's a turbulent Thursday for crypto. [Bitcoin](https://www.theblock.co/price/bitcoin) is down to around $79,000 as Binance investigates a suspected major hack involving up to $5.8 billion.

Also in today's newsletter, Polymarket resumes trading after a $2.65 million exploit, NYSE parent ICE moves to bring Hyperliquid perps to the U.S., and Utah files criminal charges against Kalshi and its executives.

Meanwhile, Curve Finance launches on Stellar, and Uniswap [opens](https://www.theblock.co/news/defi/2026-10-29-uniswap-token-jar-tjar-robinhood-432131) its fee conversion tool to apps, starting with Robinhood. [Strategy](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-10-29-strategy-q3-net-income-preferred-daily-dividends-432141) and Coinbase also posted their third-quarter earnings.

P.S. Don't forget to check out [The Latent](https://thelatent.co/), our sister website covering AI. Get The Latent Daily [here](https://thelatent.co/newsletter) and all other The Block newsletters [here](https://www.theblock.co/newsletters). Also, follow [The Block](https://x.com/TheBlockCo) and [The Latent](https://x.com/TheLatentCo) on X for more updates.

## 🚨 Binance investigating suspected hack as suspicious outflows reach up to $5.8 billion

Follow image link: (https://www.theblock.co/news/markets/2026-10-29-binance-investigating-hack-suspicious-outflows-5-billion-432171)
Caption: 

----------
Binance is investigating a potential security breach after onchain data showed billions of dollars in suspicious transfers from the crypto exchange's hot wallets.

* Onchain data flagged by analyst Spreek showed about $3.55 billion transferred to an unlabeled wallet, with nearly $900 million subsequently moved to other wallets. Coinbase's Conor Grogan estimated the amount could be as high as $5.8 billion.

* Binance co-founder Yi He said the exchange was investigating

Caption: 

# Thursday links: Election betting, the true purpose of prediction markets, Druck does perps

[The pre-history of US election betting](https://www.cfr.org/reports/betting-on-democracy)

Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour [says](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/10/26/midterms-prediction-markets-kalshi-polymarket-01135119) next week’s midterms will be the “first prediction-market election.” But a report from the Council on Foreign Relations reminds us that Americans have been betting on elections from the very start.

In 1796, for example, Federalist partisan Joab Griswold wrote that he had bet “more pounds than I am worth pence” on William Cooper winning reelection to Congress by 1,000 votes.

Cooper lost by 18 votes, which must have bankrupted Griswold.

(Note: His exact relation to Clark Griswold was impossible to verify at press time.)

By the 1880s, election betting had been "institutionalized," with specialized bookmakers setting odds from offices on Wall Street. Betting volumes soared. One [study](https://pubs.aeaweb.org/doi/pdfplus/10.1257/0895330041371277) estimates there was $6 of betting for every vote cast in the general election of 1888 (in today’s money).

In 1896, election betting is believed to have surpassed the volume of trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

In the early 1900s, the Tammany Hall political machine maintained a war chest of funds dedicated to manipulating betting odds in favor of its preferred candidates.
